key_insight: GenEHR uses a generative EHR model that accounts for irregular visit timing to forecast future cancer risk from patient health histories.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help identify patients who could benefit from risk-based screening and earlier evaluation for aggressive cancers.
method: Trained an autoregressive model on longitudinal electronic health records from millions of patients
Explicitly modeled irregular time intervals between clinical visits
Used parameter-efficient supervised adaptation to predict first cancer diagnosis within a 5-year horizon
evidence_signal: In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction performance for first cancer diagnosis over a five-year window.
watch_item: These results are retrospective, so prospective validation is needed before using it for clinical decision support or screening prioritization.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
